claims.text: The alloy under study is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Approximately 5% pre-strain followed by controlled thermal aging induces a refined dislocation-cell network.
The refined dislocation-cell network produced by optimal aging deflects propagating cracks.
The refined dislocation-cell network blunts crack tips.
Crack deflection and crack-tip blunting by the refined dislocation-cell network retain or enhance toughness.
Aging at approximately 300–500 °C for appropriate durations promotes the beneficial refined dislocation-cell structure.
Higher aging temperatures or longer aging times cause dislocation-cell coarsening.
Coarser dislocation structures are less effective at sustaining crack deflection.
Dislocation-cell coarsening caused by excessive thermal exposure reduces toughness.
A sample pre-strained by 5% and aged near 400 °C for about 5 hours will have greater toughness than the as-processed baseline.
Samples subjected to overly high aging temperatures will have lower toughness than samples aged under moderate conditions.
Samples subjected to extended aging will have lower toughness than samples aged for an intermediate duration.
Toughness will vary non-monotonically with aging temperature and duration.
The proposed behavior is expected within 300–600 °C, at approximately 5% pre-strain, and for aging durations of 1–10 hours.
Work hardening and recovery may complicate the relationship between dislocation structure and toughness.
